content.comment_body: Hello all, my location is UTC/GMT +3:30 hours. Currently, it's Friday, 27 January 2012, 18:30:59. Coordinates are roughly 35° 42' North, 51° 25' East, with sunset at 17:26 and sunrise at 07:08. I'm unable to set up the astronomical clock using a custom time zone. Appreciate any guidance.
Please share your program so we can help identify the issue.
I can set all the parameters except for the time zone. My time zone is +3:30 hours, but [product_name] does not seem to provide this option.

Hello. Unfortunately, it's not possible to use half-hour offsets in [product_name]. You must find a workaround. There was also an earlier post before the [article_no] model was released. Alternatively, you can ask in the English forum.
Hi! Simply select a time zone with GMT +3, then adjust the remaining half-hour by setting a 30-minute delay at the clock output. (Translation provided by Google as my English is not perfect)
Hello, as far as I know, time zone settings are limited to full hours in [product_name], so half-hour increments like +3:30 cannot be configured.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing issues configuring an astronomical clock with a 30-minute time zone offset in [product_name]. The software restricts adjustments to full-hour increments, making it challenging for users in time zones with half-hour differences. While some workarounds are suggested, users are frustrated by the lack of proper support.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to configure astronomical clocks using time zones with half-hour increments in [product_name], ensuring accurate setup for their locations.
pain_keywords: lack of half-hour time zone option
